method: Offered traffic A in erlangs is busy-hour calls multiplied by average handle time in seconds, divided by 3600. For N agents, first evaluate Erlang B with B(0) = 1 and B(n) = A x B(n-1) / (n + A x B(n-1)). When N is greater than A, Erlang C queue probability is C = B(N) / (1 - (A/N) x (1 - B(N))). Average wait across all calls is C x H/(N-A), average wait once queued is H/(N-A), and service level within t seconds is 1 - C x exp(-(N-A) x t/H), where H is average handle time. At or above full occupancy (N less than or equal to A), no steady-state queue probability, wait or service level is reported. The target agent count is the smallest stable N up to 1,500 whose service level meets the entered percentage. Inputs allow up to 36,000 calls/hour and 3,600-second handle times, with offered load capped at 1,000 erlangs. This planning estimate assumes Poisson arrivals, exponential handle times, identical agents, an unlimited queue and no abandonment or retries; it reports concurrent agents before shrinkage, not roster headcount.

sources.title: Erlang C delay formula for an M/M/N queue: C = B / (1 - (A/N)(1-B)), where B is the corresponding Erlang B blocking probability and N > A
M/M/N waiting-time distribution: service level within t seconds is 1 - C exp(-(N-A)t/H), with mean handle time H and offered load A
Erlang as a unit of traffic intensity: busy-hour calls x mean handle time / 3600
